Sidebar drag-to-reorder

Throwaway HTML so contributors can feel the reorder before porting it to production UI. Native dragstart / dragover / drop, keyboard move controls, no libraries, and no sibling assets.

Drag a row with the pointer, or use each row's Move up and Move down buttons. The current order is shown below the list.

  • InboxMoving Untriaged drafts and reviewer notes
  • Today3Moving Drafts due in the current review window
  • Upcoming21Moving Queued edits that are scheduled but not active

No row is being moved.

What you are feeling

Design decisions baked into this prototype, so reviewers can push back on them.

  • Drop indicator snaps to the nearest gap, not the raw cursor Y. It only moves when the pointer crosses a row midpoint, which feels more decisive and less jittery.
  • Dragged row stays in place at 48% opacity with a 2deg tilt, dashed outline, and visible Moving label. Keeping the original row in the list preserves the starting position; the tilt reads as lifted.
  • Grip dots are the affordance, but the whole row is draggable. Dots teach the gesture without forcing a tiny hit target, while buttons provide the complete keyboard route.
  • No auto-scroll, no drop animation. Left out on purpose so the core feel is easy to judge before adding motion around the edges.

Open questions

  1. Should Trash and maybe Archive be pinned to the bottom and excluded from reordering?
  2. Do we want rows to slide to their new slot on drop, or is the instant snap acceptable?
  3. Keyboard path: is Alt + Arrow to move the focused row enough for the first ship?
